slot_note: re-root after the platform landed architecture 3 (both runs on the golden at every ask); one architecture per world, so a new world (a sand-plain well field in central Wisconsin), dataset (nitrate laboratory results, a county groundwater network under its parcels' land-cover histories, a wellhead protection model's parcel table) and shell (docx, xlsx and png, a when-question)
niche: a city water utility's nitrate removal plant under the 10 mg/L nitrate-N standard at its well field's entry point: whether the plant must go into the state loan program's 2027 cycle or can wait for the 2031 cycle, from the blended nitrate the well field will deliver from 2027 to 2040 (Sulfur task type: physical-model calibration and data assimilation; spatiotemporal exposure and source apportionment)
answer: Apply in the 2027 cycle: the blended entry-point nitrate first reaches 10 mg/L as N in 2031, three years before a plant funded in 2031 could enter service, because the ridge timber cleared for irrigated vegetables from 2016 to 2020 has not yet leached through 60 to 90 ft of sand to the water table.
analyst_test: With the lab results converted to nitrate-N, the county lab's reporting limits and the re-keyed duplicates sorted, the easy route reads each well's annual means (flat near 7 since 2019), finds the ridge clearing in the protection area's land cover, expects its leachate over the wellhead model's groundwater travel time (one to four years) or over one lag fitted to the wells' own history (six to nine years), sees no rise at Wells 6 and 7 or at the county wells under recent clearings, sets the clearing's effect near nil and files the 2031 cycle with the blend under 8.5 through 2040; it never times each parcel's leachate through its own unsaturated thickness, which the county's older conversions show stepping up later the deeper the water table.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a well field's nitrate over the next decade, worked the way groundwater-quality forecasting works it: nitrate leached under each parcel's land cover, carried down through the unsaturated sand at a pace set by its moisture and its recharge, then through the aquifer to the wells over the groundwater travel time, and mixed at each well in proportion to each parcel's recharge; with a clinic's or a retailer's nouns there is no water table, no unsaturated zone and no recharge to mix, so the task stops making sense.
layer1: nitrate reported as nitrate-N by one lab and as nitrate (mg/L NO3) by the county health lab before 2004, with '<' values at two reporting limits
samples re-keyed when the utility's SCADA renamed the wells, field duplicates and lab re-runs as extra rows, entry-point samples beside raw-water samples
the county network's site IDs re-issued when two wells were replaced, sites with gaps and a dry-season skip year
the land-cover panel's local codes before 2008 and cropland-layer codes after, parcels split and re-numbered by the assessor
SCADA daily pumping in gallons then thousand gallons after a meter change, missing days, a duplicated export week
the age survey's tritium-helium ages for water-table wells and the production wells' mixed ages
stakeholder_role: Wexmoor Water Utility's general manager, preparing the utility commission's loan-cycle decision

spine.entity: one well-day of pumping; one parcel-year of land cover
spine.grain: well x day; parcel x year

world.geography: United States, Wisconsin (Tarrow County, a fictional county on the central sand plain; Wexmoor, a fictional city)
world.org_type: a city water utility, its utility commission and a county land and water conservation department
invented_names: Tarrow County Land and Water Conservation Department

driver: The decisive quantity is a blended output's level over the coming years, fed by inputs whose change at the source travels through a stage no measurement of the output or of the medium sees, at a pace set by each source's own depth through that stage; a recent change sits on sources deeper than the earlier changes that matured, so the output's own history, one delay fitted to it, the downstream travel time a filed model gives, and an event study on the recent change all show no effect and set it near nil, and only the matured changes' delays, read against each source's depth and carried to each recent source, show the rise arriving inside the decision window.
driver_concrete: Each year's 2027 to 2040 entry-point nitrate is the pumping plan's blend of Wells 5, 6 and 7, each a recharge-weighted mix of its protection-area parcels' water-table nitrate delayed by the wellhead model's groundwater travel time, where a parcel's water-table nitrate is its land cover's leachate delayed by its unsaturated thickness times the sand's moisture over the recharge; the Holcomb Ridge parcels cleared for irrigated vegetables from 2016 to 2020 sit over 60 to 90 ft of sand, so their leachate reaches the wells from 2028 to 2031, not by 2024 as the travel time or the wells' own lag would put it.
stump: A strong analyst who finds the ridge clearing tests it against the wells and the county wells under recent clearings, sees no rise where the wellhead model's travel time or the wells' own fitted lag says it should already be, sets the clearing's effect near nil and files the 2031 cycle with the blend under 8.5 through 2040; only each parcel's delay through its own unsaturated thickness, read from the county's older conversions, puts the rise at the wells from 2028 and the blend at 10 in 2031.
deep_chain: (1) the wells' falling-then-flat record is the nutrient-management era's water arriving and cannot show leachate still above the water table; (2) the county's older conversions step up after a delay that grows with depth to water (the unsaturated travel time), while the water-table wells' own ages are one to two years, so the delay is in the unsaturated sand, not the aquifer; (3) the ridge parcels' delays follow from their 60 to 90 ft of sand, against the 15 to 40 ft the matured conversions and the wells' farmland sit on, so no pooled delay applies; (4) the irrigated-vegetable leachate after nutrient management, from the network, and each parcel's share of its well's water by recharge (irrigated land recharges more than forest); (5) the pumping plan's blend from 2027 with Well 3 retired, and the first year at 10
judgment: separating 'the clearing does not raise nitrate' from 'its leachate has not arrived' with the matured conversions' delays against depth to water, and carrying a depth-specific delay, not a pooled one, to the ridge parcels
one_fact_test: 'the ridge clearing will raise nitrate' rescues nothing: with the wellhead model's travel time or the wells' fitted lag the rise should already show, it does not, and the reasonable fit sets it near nil; the delay must be built from each parcel's unsaturated thickness and read from the matured conversions

differentiation.mark181: mark181 nowcasts each area's specimens from each courier route's own reporting delay; here nothing is reported: a physical input travels through an unobserved stage at a pace set by each source's depth, and the delay is read from earlier land-cover changes that matured, not from a reporting log
differentiation.mark166: mark166 v3 forecasts new customers through departures linked across groups at a lagged yield; here no record links a source to the output: the delay is a physical travel time through a stage nothing samples, set by each parcel's depth to water, and the recent change sits deeper than the matured ones
differentiation.mark451: mark451 completes claims whose handler delay collapsed partway; here the delay never changed for any source, it differs across sources with their depth, and the recent sources sit deeper than every matured one
differentiation.task3: task3 v1 carried each earlier move's gain conditioned on a covariate its history printed, which both runs did by reflex; here the decisive step comes before any conditioning: the recent change's absent response is read as not yet arrived rather than as no effect, because the delay sits in a stage no record samples and the matured changes alone time it
differentiation.mark234: mark234 reads each laboratory's current output from a share a loss in transit cannot move; here nothing is lost: every unit of the input arrives, late by a travel time set by each source's depth, and the decisive step separates an effect not yet arrived from no effect at all

lineage.driver: The extra input an upgraded service level puts into a unit is the part of the unit the old level left untreated, so the average gain measured on units upgraded earlier, chosen because the old level already treated much of them, understates the gain for units the old level barely reached, while their upgraded level less the new units' present input overstates it; only the gain conditioned on how much of each unit the old level already treated, read from each unit's own record under it, carries across to the new units.
lineage.stump: A competent solver takes the Priority 1 collectors' salt per lane-km per severity point less the 424 lane-km's own Priority 2 salt and files 2,600 t at the planning severity, or takes the before-and-after gain of the collectors moved to Priority 1 since 2022 and files 1,500 to 1,600 t; the step that lands it there is carrying an average across streets whose Priority 2 coverage differs, when the gain is the length Priority 2 left untreated and the earlier moves were mostly hill, school and inner-suburb streets Priority 2 had already salted along much of their length, so only the gain conditioned on each street's own Priority 2 salt files 2,200 t.
lineage.driver_concrete: Quellbrook's Priority 2 trucks salt a collector only at its intersections, hills and curves, so a collector's gain on moving to Priority 1 is mostly the stretch between them at the Priority 1 rate; the collectors moved from 2022 to 2025 were mostly hill, school and hospital-access streets whose Priority 2 salt already covered much of their length, while the redesign's 424 lane-km are long flat outer-suburb grid collectors whose Priority 2 trucks salted about a sixth of them, so the moved streets' average gain understates theirs and the Priority 1 collectors' rate less the new streets' own Priority 2 salt overstates it; only the gain read off each moved street's own Priority 2 salt, at the new streets' Priority 2 salt, carries across.
lineage.fate: landed on the portal (2026-11-07): one response filed the golden 2,200 t by regressing each earlier move's gain on its own Priority 2 salt and reading it at the new streets' (100 per cent), the other filed the default 2,600 t and still kept 70 per cent on the asks; conditioning a carried gain on a covariate each unit's history prints is the strong solver's reflex, so the world is spent
spent 2026-11-08 on the platform: both runs bounded the tank's dewatering by the Southside plant's hourly headroom and landed Alternative C and every ask (REDESIGN)
lineage.driver: A storage buffer that captures a discharge until it is full empties only through a receiving channel whose spare capacity vanishes for one to several days after each wet event, so in a run of events the buffer meets the next one still partly full; counting each event against an empty buffer, or a buffer emptied at its outlet's rated pace, understates how often it spills, and only replaying the record with the outlet bounded by the receiving channel's spare capacity, read from that channel's own record, prices the size the limit needs.
lineage.driver_concrete: Clay Street's tank is pumped out into the Southside interceptor at the plant headworks, and the Southside plant, its sewershed full of groundwater and inflow, takes its 140 MGD hydraulic limit for one to four days after most storms from March to June; the Northside tank, whose plant has room within hours, empties at its pumps' rating and its overflows replay exactly that way, but Clay Street's pumps can only send what Southside has room for, so in a wet spell the tank meets the next storm still full and the 26 MG alternative that clears four events at its pumps' rating leaves 6.8 a year; only the 38 MG tank, at 2.9, meets the decree.
lineage.stump: A competent solver replays Outfall 014's metered overflows through each tank pumped out at its station's rated dewatering flow (the continuous simulation the decree evaluates by, which reproduces the Northside tank's overflows since 2020) and selects Alternative B, the 26 MG tank, at 2.8 events a year; the step that lands it there is taking the pumps' rating as the pace the tank empties, when it empties into the Southside interceptor at the headworks of a plant that sits at its 140 MGD limit for days after wet-season storms, so only a replay bounded by Southside's own headroom hour by hour shows the 20 MG tank at 6.8 events and selects Alternative C, the 38 MG tank, at 2.9.
lineage.answer: Select Alternative C, the 38 MG tank: it leaves Outfall 014 2.9 untreated overflow events a year, where the 26 MG Alternative B leaves 6.8.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a long-horizon response to a sustained load, when a short trial's response carries two opposing far-field effects that cancel inside its window and part only over years: the trial's own model fits it closely and overstates the long response, so the far field must be calibrated on the record a nearby load has already left, read against a natural baseline from references beyond that load's reach, because the nearest reference sits inside it and a fitted trend absorbs the response.
lineage.stump: A strong analyst who sees the test's Theis forecast overshoot the Mill Street record recalibrates the leakage against the nearest network well CV-07 (or the wells' own pre-pumping levels, or a fitted trend) and files 1,250 gpm, every schedule under 3.5 ft at OW-S; only the natural level carried from CV-02 and CV-11 beyond the cone files 1,000 gpm.
lineage.answer: File the 1,000 gpm schedule: its greatest monthly drawdown at OW-S in 2046 is 8 ft against the 9 ft limit, where 1,250 gpm reaches 10 ft.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-08 on the platform: both runs fitted a leaky strip with the plate's walls to the test, took CV-02 and CV-11 beyond the cone as natural-level controls, and landed Schedule C and every ask (REDESIGN)
